transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03 16:12 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel, Rhea Coleman, Jorge Kim (Redwood); Alyssa Chen, Marco Ruiz, Priya Nair, Ben Lowe (Edenware)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Kickoff for pilot onboarding. Discussed success metrics (latency, cost, quality), options for OpenAI-compatible endpoints vs Redwood SDK direct integration, structured output and function-calling needs, benchmarks and timeline. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule a bench kick-off.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, Samir from Redwood, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Alyssa: Hi, Alyssa here.
[00:07] Marco: Marco Ruiz.
[00:09] Priya: Priya Nair, Infosec.
[00:11] Ben: Ben Lowe, product.
[00:12] Rhea: Rhea Coleman, SE. Jorge on the call too.
[00:15] Jorge: Hey all.
[00:18] Samir: Cool. Agenda — scope the pilot so we can land a 6-week sprint: success criteria, traffic sizing, benchmark plan, and an integration path. We hear you're evaluating both OpenAI-compatible endpoints and direct Redwood SDK integration; correct?
[00:33] Alyssa: Yeah that's right. We want minimal dev friction + predictable cost.
[00:36] Ben: And structured output — we need JSON responses for our inventory assistant, tool calling to hit internal product APIs, and a clear fallback when latency spikes.
[00:45] Rhea: Got it. Can you share the core success metrics up front? What are you measuring?
[00:49] Ben: For us: 1) 99th percentile latency under 600ms for short prompts (~128 tokens), 2) cost under $0.06 per 1k tokens in steady-state, and 3) >= 85% accuracy on our three eval sets. If those hold, we consider pilot successful.
[01:07] Marco: To add, throughput matters: we have bursts up to 250 qps during peak. Steady-state is 20–30 qps.
[01:15] Samir: That burst profile is really helpful. For the pilot we usually run both a latency-sensitive config (pinned small model on dedicated pool) and a cheaper batch-friendly config to compare. For clarity: are you leaning towards hosted API (OpenAI-compatible endpoints) or embedding Redwood SDK in your infra?
[01:31] Alyssa: Prefer hosted to start for speed, but if we see data residency or compliance blockers we may pivot to private deployment.
[01:38] Priya: Security wise, SOC2 and audit logs are musts; we also need SSO via SAML and KMS integration for any keys.
[01:46] Rhea: Understood. Redwood supports SSO, audit logs, and KMS. We'll include docs.
[01:50] Jorge: Quick note on function/tool calling: we support OpenAI-compatible function calling. It's basically the same pattern but we add structured output helpers and a schema validation layer in the SDK.
[02:02] Ben: Schema validation layer — can you elaborate?
[02:05] Jorge: Sure. When you define a function, the SDK will validate the model's response JSON against the function schema; if mismatch, we surface the diff and optionally auto-retry with a system hint. Helps reduce downstream parsing errors.
[02:19] Marco: That sounds useful. Our product wants to call internal 'getInventory' and 'reserveStock' endpoints, and we need strong guarantees about arg types.
[02:28] Rhea: We'll map out a sample flow. For the pilot we suggest three integration patterns: 1) OpenAI-compatible endpoints with recent OpenAI-compat SDK calls, 2) Redwood SDK direct (server-side) for lower latency and richer telemetry, 3) a hybrid where you use hosted endpoints for dev and switch to Dedicated for peaks.
[02:47] Alyssa: For the bench we want to measure all three.
[02:50] Samir: Great. On benchmarks — we ask customers to provide anonymized traffic traces and eval prompt sets. We'll run: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost estimates (with and without caching/prefix caching), function-calling success rates, and structured-output validation pass rate. We'll provide a results sheet.
[03:10] Marco: What does the harness look like? Is it something we run, or you run it in your infra?
[03:14] Rhea: We do both. For baseline we'll run in Redwood-hosted test infra against your sample traffic; then we'll hand you the harness (scripted JMeter or python locust + Redwood SDK examples) so you can reproduce. The harness will simulate your burst profile and our continuous batching behavior.
[03:29] Ben: Any special prep for function calling in the harness?
[03:32] Jorge: We'll include function definitions and a mocked internal API to validate end-to-end. The harness will check types and response shapes. There may be some noise in transcripts — sorry, mixing metaphors — but you'll get a pass/fail and detailed diffs.
[03:47] Priya: On encryption: we require CMEK for keys in any dedicated/private deployment. Hosted is okay if you offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with HSM-backed KMS.
[03:59] Samir: Redwood supports BYOK and HSM integrations for Private; for Hosted we can offer customer-managed keys via our KMS partners — we'll surface the documentation and limitations.
[04:10] Alyssa: Do you have benchmarks for quantized models? Some of our data is longer context (~2k tokens) and cost matters.
[04:18] Rhea: Yes — we have profiles for 2k contexts and quantized variants; for long contexts batching effects are different. We'll recommend model/quantization combos per workload. We'll include recommended kernel/profile.
[04:30] Marco: Can we target the first benchmark run within two weeks?
[04:33] Samir: If we get sample traffic and eval sets by Friday (8/7) we can run an initial bench that week and share results the following week — so that aligns with a 6-week pilot to finish by mid-September.
[04:45] Ben: That timeline works.
[04:47] Jorge: A note on routing and fallbacks — our runtime supports policy-based routing; if a dedicated pool is saturated we can fall back to a compatible model in the hosted tier. We'll show the policy config in the SOW.
[04:59] Priya: For auditability we need request/response logs for 30 days, and redaction options for PII. Do you redact at rest or on ingest?
[05:07] Rhea: We support redaction on ingest and configurable retention windows; audit logs are immutable and exportable to your SIEM. We'll include the SOC2 section in the packet.
[05:18] Alyssa: How does pricing look for a pilot with 2 dedicated GPUs during peaks?
[05:22] Samir: We'll share pricing bands; pilot pricing is usually a reduced reserved capacity + overage tiers. I'll send illustrative numbers, but the benchmark will give you a better cost per 1k token estimate once we run it.
[05:33] Marco: Regarding SDKs — do you maintain official SDKs for Node/Python/Go?
[05:36] Rhea: Node and Python are first-class; Go has a community SDK maintained by Redwood DK team. All SDKs support OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling helpers, streaming, and structured output validation. We'll attach example snippets in the follow-up email.
[05:50] Ben: We use Typescript heavily. Any example for tool calling and error-handling?
[05:54] Jorge: Yes. Example: define function schemas in TS, call via the SDK, get a typed response or an error object with diff info. We'll include a short sample repo link.
[06:05] Samir: I'm going to summarize the pilot scope — please interrupt if I miss anything. 1) Prep: Edenware provides traffic and eval sets; Redwood shares harness and security docs. 2) Benchmarks: run three permutations (hosted compat endpoint, Redwood SDK direct, hybrid/dedicated) measuring latency (p95/p99), cost proxies, batching efficiency, and structured-output pass rate. 3) Integration: wire up function calling for two internal APIs and validate schema. 4) Timeline: initial bench run within two weeks, iterate, finalize pilot results by ~2026-09-15.
[06:35] Alyssa: That's accurate.
[06:37] Priya: Need to review the SOC2/architecture before we spin up any test infra — can you send that by Wednesday?
[06:43] Samir: We'll send the security pack by 2026-08-05.
[06:46] Ben: For acceptance criteria, do you require a signed SOW before we start running benches?
[06:50] Samir: Typically we exchange a light pilot SOW to cover reserved capacity and data handling; we can run an initial non-production bench against anonymized samples before SOW if you prefer.
[06:59] Marco: We'll opt for anonymized baseline first. If results look good we sign the SOW.
[07:04] Rhea: Cool. Any technical constraints we should know about?
[07:07] Marco: We have a legacy product API that only speaks protobuf over gRPC, and some of our telemetry pipelines expect newline-delimited JSON.
[07:15] Jorge: No problem — SDKs can handle JSON/protobuf mapping; we'll include example adapter code.
[07:21] Alyssa: On structured output: can we enforce a strict schema so the model won't hallucinate fields?
[07:26] Rhea: We'll use schema validation and system prompts to bias output; combined with the SDK's retry-on-mismatch policy it's pretty robust. Not 100% bulletproof, but the validation step reduces downstream errors a lot.
[07:38] Ben: What about streaming partial structured responses? We sometimes want to show progressive results to the user.
[07:42] Jorge: Streaming works with structured output; the SDK emits partial JSON tokens and an incremental validator. If the final result fails validation, the harness will flag it, and you can choose to fall back to last-known-good or re-request.
[07:55] Priya: A couple security clarifications: do you support IP allowlists for callbacks, and can logs be forwarded to our Splunk instance?
[07:62] Samir: (laughs) that's 07:62, funny — yes, IP allowlists for webhooks and log forwarding to Splunk/Datadog via syslog/HTTP ingest are supported. We'll document endpoints and cert requirements.
[08:12] Alyssa: Great. Anything else on timelines?
[08:14] Samir: We'll shoot for the following milestones: 1) 8/05: security + pricing + harness, 2) 8/07: Edenware shares data, 3) 8/10–8/14: first benchmark run, 4) 8/17: sync to review results and decide SOW next steps.
[08:30] Ben: Works for us.
[08:32] Marco: One more question — in the event of a model regression during the pilot, do you have rollback/monitoring hooks?
[08:38] Rhea: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval monitoring and automatic rollback to previous model snapshot if we see regressions on your control prompt set. We'll wire up alerting to your Slack/PagerDuty channels.
[08:52] Priya: Please include retention policies for logs and the option to turn off storage after the pilot.
[08:57] Samir: Noted. We'll include that in the SOW addendum.
[09:01] Alyssa: Okay, if no other questions, let's recap next steps.
[09:05] Samir: Recap: Redwood sends benchmark template, security pack, pricing examples, and sample SDK snippets by 8/5. Edenware provides anonymized traffic and eval prompt sets by 8/7. Schedule bench kick-off for week of 8/10.
[09:18] Ben: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:21] Marco: Thanks.
[09:23] Priya: Thanks.
[09:24] Samir: Appreciate it, talk soon.
